Counter-evidence that caps the driver case: of 124 raw findings, driver_would_prevent is 'no' for 62 and 'partially' for 27; armature-bug is the single largest root cause at 36. The highest-severity class survives both architectures: false-green test suites, 8 raw findings, P0. Struct-only tests hid a string-vs-int enum mismatch that made the reviewer-to-record loop non-functional; hollow assertions let `arm worktree list`/`gc` be a total no-op through multiple PR review rounds on #89 because the test computed the path the same wrong way production did. The repo already runs coverage and 100% mutation efficacy and these passed anyway. The LLM authors the tests and the gates run them green under either driver.

Armature already was the deterministic driver. E7-S1 (2026-05-08) shipped `arm orchestrate` and `arm worker run` with launch adapters for claude/codex/devin (ce6f7273), crash-resume state derivation (c9991c6c), and zero-trust diff/reset/stage/commit. The whole subsystem was deleted on 2026-06-04 (70c0d3b5, 45d05dfe, ab29ce6c) with the recorded rationale 'managed execution was abandoned because harness behavior and inversion of control created excessive complexity' and the standing non-goal 'Do not add a replacement run, execute, dispatch, or handoff command' (/home/brian/development/armature/docs/archive/orchestration/2026-06-03-remove-managed-execution-design.md, verified present). 19 of the corpus's 29 cancellations are debris of that arc, and ADR 0009 ratified the constitution after the kill, encoding it as N2 and T1.

Seams work when they rule on facts agents control, and the record shows the conversion pattern repeatedly: heartbeats went from prompt instructions (E5-S1-T13) to hook-automated (LNGHZN-S3); PR discipline from skill prose to a transition gate (task-1774961009); gate results from prose claims to hash-anchored evidence ops (LNGHZN-S10-T3, ADR 0014's 'reported is not evidenced'); warnings to errors with escape hatches deleted (ADR 0016). The citation validator caught every hallucinated line number in the corpus, and contract-mandated _REQ_ test names forced e2e tests that surfaced a real path bug on LNGHZN-S3-T1.

Seams that rule on facts agents do NOT control actively corrode enforcement, and a driver inherits this. arm doctor D8 flags ~16 harness-injected /dev/null bind-mounted dotfiles as out-of-scope violations, three recurrences over four weeks, clean only with the sandbox disabled — 'a check which is always red is a check nobody reads.' False-positive overlap warnings trained coordinators to pass --force on every claim (11 consecutive on DF-S5). ADR 0016 records agents routing around a slow whole-graph validate onto check-fast: 'Fail-closed on paper, fail-open in practice.'

The harness cannot be the hard seam. PreToolUse exit code 2 is a genuine non-overridable block on file writes, but it does not intercept a model calling `arm transition --to done` directly, and ADR 0007 plus /home/brian/development/armature/docs/harness-hook.md make every hook resolution failure deliberately fail-open — 'the hook is a best-effort guardrail, not a sandbox.' ADR 0016 explicitly rejected 'a harness hook as the primary control (Claude-shaped; I5).' Hard enforcement must live in arm's own verbs and write doors, which is equally available under either architecture.

The commercial constraint that killed the driver has not moved: `claude --print` requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and Anthropic's 2026 policy bans subscription OAuth tokens in third-party contexts. A driver architecture therefore forces per-token API billing on every armature user and re-couples the product to per-vendor harness adapters — the exact addressable-market shrink cited in the original abandonment. Meanwhile the prompted layer is the corpus's primary hole-finder: ~60 commits exist solely to address review cycles, the fix/broad-review/implement cascade is confirmed across 10+ runs on PRs #66/69/70/71/108, and holistic LLM review found P0 bugs on three stories that deterministic gates structurally could not see — including a bug inside a shipped deterministic seam (IsWithinScope failing to strip the ' (new)' annotation).
risks: The seam path has been reactive, and that is the strongest argument against this recommendation. Every seam in the record shipped only after its failure class burned a story, and ARCHIMP-S15 sat undetected for months precisely because the needed check was on a follow-up list rather than in the transition path. If the candidate follow-ups from the eight themes are not front-loaded as tracked, scheduled work with a burn-down, D-without-launch degrades into A with better intentions and the next P0 lands the same way.

Seam complexity may eventually exceed driver complexity. LNGHZN-S4 cost 38 fix commits to 3 feat, with three distinct bypasses of the same gate inside nine days, and LNGHZN-S9-T1 took 1 feat plus 10 fix on a single task. If the fix-per-seam ratio does not fall as control-plane authority consolidates, the whack-a-mole reading wins and the ORCRMV complexity verdict should be revisited on its own terms.

The recommendation assumes a human or an interactive session is present to invoke the verbs. If the actual product target is unattended autonomous runs — no one at the keyboard — then D-without-launch is structurally insufficient, because someone must still call `arm sync` or `arm merged`. In that world C or D-with-launch is correct and the constitution needs an amending ADR. This is a product-positioning question the evidence cannot settle, and it should be answered explicitly before Stage 3.

Harness vendors can move the ground unilaterally. The D8 case is the proof: a sandbox bind-mount changed what a deterministic gate sees, and it stayed broken across three recurrences with no fix available on the arm side. Session default cwd, hook semantics, tool rosters, and sandbox mount behavior are all vendor-controlled. Any arm-side determinism whose correctness depends on harness environment facts will keep degrading, and a driver would have absorbed some of this by running gates in an un-sandboxed parent — a real advantage this recommendation gives up.

The recommendation does nothing about the highest-severity class. Hollow tests mirroring production bugs, semantic reverts merging cleanly, and requirements silently unmet under plausible code are unaddressed by control-plane authority, and they are P0. If those dominate real-world cost, the entire driver-versus-seams debate is a second-order argument and the correct investment is review architecture — mandatory whole-story holistic review before PR, cross-story scope-overlap detection, patch-id content audits — rather than either option under assessment.

The evidence base is one repo, one operator, one workflow, and heavily haiku-tier implementers; the self-report theme notes every fabrication instance involved a haiku worker. A meaningful share of the protocol-failure class may be model-capability-bound rather than architecture-bound, in which case building a driver would be paying permanent structural cost to solve a temporary problem. Conversely, if the target deployment is cheap-model fleets, the protocol class is permanent and the driver case strengthens.

Consolidating control-plane authority in arm concentrates blast radius. Today a wrong transition corrupts one issue's record; a deterministic promoter that derives merged from patch-id comparison across the whole DAG can be wrong systematically and silently, and the same two-valued reporting habit that produced 'No merged branches detected' would then be making merge decisions at scale. The third-value work in Stage 2 is a precondition for Stage 1, not a follow-on.

The 27 percent hardening-tax figure that indicts A is partly an artifact of measurement. Much of armature's remaining work is agent-governance functionality — that is the product — so the line between 'compensating for bad drivers' and 'building the thing' is genuinely blurred. If the tax is overstated, A is less damning than the synthesis presents; if the stricter reading is right and trust machinery is past half the corpus, the case for rethinking the whole product boundary is stronger than any of the four options address.
draft_verdict.recommendation:
Adopt Option D-without-launch — armature takes deterministic authority over the control plane and never executes a model — reached in four stages. The governing rule to write down first, because it settles every subsequent argument: no governance step may be optional-by-prompt. Agents may drive work; they may not own facts.

STAGE 0 — stop recording fiction (days, before any other work). Four changes, all pure git facts, all I5-clean, no LLM in the loop. (1) `arm transition --to merged` refuses without content-on-main evidence, or the path is removed entirely so merged is reachable only through `arm merged`. (2) RunRollup in /home/brian/development/armature/internal/materialize/engine.go:589 verifies rather than aggregates. (3) Add the doctor check the unknown-recorded-as-answered theme calls its single highest-value item: for every merged issue, is its declared scope's content on origin/main? It would have caught ARCHIMP-S15 at any point in two months. (4) Fix SkippedDeliveryGate:false — never write a positive assertion for a check that did not execute. Stage 0 is the minimum bar for a system whose central claim is I6.

STAGE 1 — close the loop without an agent typing anything (weeks). Persist the derived branch on the claim op, mirroring the shipped worktree_path precedent (f13bcb5a), and stop asking agents for --branch — zero ops carried it across an entire story, and no skill sentence will change that. Make `arm sync` decide merged from git evidence including squash merges, pull-only so T3 stays clear, and report what it did not examine ("N done issues skipped: no branch recorded") alongside its verdict. Gate `arm merged` on the presence — never the rating — of a conformance assessment, with `--i7-override --reason` as the only bypass, ordered before worktree teardown so the command that discovers the gap does not also close the recovery window.

STAGE 2 — make honesty an invariant, and fix the seams that lie (weeks, partly parallel). Introduce the third value in the data model: checked-true, checked-false, not-checked, with not-checked rendering as not-checked everywhere. Add a review-time rule for the pattern the S18 finding names — seam-deepening refactors converting loud failures into silent skips (`verifyResults, _ := lc.VerifyAll()`). Then repair the seams that rule on facts agents cannot control, because these are what train agents to distrust gates: D8 confined to paths the repo could plausibly own or sandbox-aware; CleanTree honoring .gitignore so running the mandatory gate does not fail the gate; the overlap checker given transitive closure, parent-containment, and glob matching so --force stops being reflex. Every one of these is deterministic and in-architecture.

STAGE 3 — a pre-registered decision point, not an open question. After Stages 0-2 have one full story of data, re-evaluate Option C against a single criterion agreed in advance: does a new class of protocol failure appear that cannot be closed by a refusal at a verb? If yes, write the amending ADR — in the narrow, upgrade-only style of ADR 0008 — for a re-entrant `arm run --once` step function: foreground, human-launched, exits between steps, state only in git ops, crash-safe by materialization. Never a supervisor, never a daemon, and never model invocation inside arm. Keep harness launching in a thin external runner the user owns, so N2 and ADR 0005 stay intact and API-key billing remains the user's choice rather than armature's requirement. If no such class appears, C stays killed and the ORCRMV record stands.

CROSS-CUTTING, and the part most likely to be skipped: take the candidate follow-up lists from all eight themes and file them as one tracked epic with an explicit burn-down. The record is unambiguous that follow-up lists are where P0s go to wait — that is how ARCHIMP-S15 survived. Also keep the LLM review cascade exactly as it is: it is the corpus's most-confirmed working pattern, it found bugs inside your own deterministic seams, and nothing in this plan replaces it. Make the whole-story holistic pass a required pre-PR step rather than an optional one, which is the one place where a mandatory gate and LLM judgment should be deliberately combined.

attacks.claim_attacked: "Arithmetic: driver_would_prevent is 'no' for 62 of 124 raw findings" — the first of four pillars rejecting Option C.
attacks.refutation: The draft divides by the wrong denominator. The evidence block itself carries two distributions: `by_driver_would_prevent` {no:62, yes:35, partially:27} over all 124 findings, and `negative_by_driver_would_prevent` {no:46, yes:35, partially:25} over the 106 negatives. 18 of the 124 are `positive_count` findings — things that went right — where "would a driver have prevented this" is a null question, and all 16 of the difference land in the "no" bucket. Scored against actual problems, a driver fully or partially prevents 60 of 106 (57%), a clear majority, not the minority-of-124 the draft presents. The draft's own most-cited classes are the ones the field marks yes: the worker-worktree-bypass family (5-7 recurrences), fabricated-done, the parallel git checkout race, worker-left-task-claimed, skip-full-make-check. Second-order: `driver_would_prevent` is a self-assessed field written by the same prompted LLMs whose reliability is under examination, in findings authored mostly before a driver was under consideration — it is the weakest possible evidence to hang a keystone count on, and the draft treats it as arithmetic.

attacks.claim_attacked: "armature-bug is the largest root cause at 36 — a driver runs the same buggy arm code and fails identically."
attacks.refutation: Inspect what those bugs are. The exemplars the draft itself names — `isClaimedWorktreeForIssue` probing the invoking checkout (2026-08-02T1600Z), `IsWithinScope` failing to strip ' (new)' (2026-07-25T2330Z), the DAG-blind overlap checker (2026-06-30T2200Z), CleanTree counting gitignored artifacts (2026-08-09T1510Z), hand-rolled merge-base picking stale main — are not general-purpose armature logic. They are guardrail code that exists only because an untrusted driver has to be policed after the fact. A process that owns cwd, branch, and commit does not need to infer the claimed worktree from the invoking checkout; the check, and therefore its bug, does not exist. The draft counts the maintenance cost of Option B's compensating machinery as evidence against Option C. That is circular: the treadmill is the artifact of the architecture being defended, and the corpus shows the treadmill generating its own P0s (an LLM review pass found a bug *inside* a shipped deterministic seam — the draft cites this approvingly without noticing it indicts B).

attacks.claim_attacked: "Commercial 3/10 … --print requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, subscription OAuth is banned … the exact addressable-market shrink cited in the original abandonment."
attacks.refutation: Two failures. (1) The attribution is fabricated. `docs/archive/orchestration/2026-06-03-remove-managed-execution-design.md` contains no mention of API keys, billing, subscriptions, addressable market, or cost of any kind — `rg -i 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|api key|subscription|billing|market'` over that file returns nothing. Its recorded rationale is exactly one thing: "harness behavior and inversion of control created excessive complexity" (line 294-295). The draft attaches a 2026-era commercial argument to a 2026-06 decision that did not make it, then calls it "the constraint that killed it the first time," which is a citation to a document that says otherwise. (2) The underlying fact is misstated. The draft's own source (`docs/design/determinism-review/evidence-bundle.json`) reads: "When using --print with OAuth (no API key), billing is per-token API usage, not subscription; this is by design, not a restriction. There is NO current documented restriction on --print itself." That is a billing-mode statement, not a ban. And it is irrelevant to the half of Option C that matters: a state-machine step function that owns git/cwd/transition/gate-execution mechanics launches no model at all and has zero billing surface. The draft's own Stage 3 concedes this by proposing "a thin external runner the user owns" — which proves the billing objection is about who owns the launch script, not about whether arm owns the state machine. One of four pillars is a miscitation; a second is scoped to a capability C does not require.

attacks.claim_attacked: "ADR 0005's standing 'will not run models inside Armature'" and "direct N2 collision … T1 in spirit if not letter" — Constitutional fit 3/10 for C.
attacks.refutation: ADR 0005 says, verbatim: "**Phase one** will not run models or customer checks inside Armature." Phase-scoped, not standing. The draft upgrades a phase boundary into a permanent prohibition and scores against it. On the constitution proper: T1/T2/T3 are the tripwires — long-running process, history rewrite, bidirectional mutable-remote sync — and the draft concedes a foreground `arm run --once` trips none of them ("in spirit if not letter" is an admission that the letter is clean). What remains is N2, a *non-goal*, and non-goals are the soft layer the house convention explicitly amends by ADR. Meanwhile the draft never scores C against the invariants it satisfies best: I4 (agents are the primary users — a driver is the maximally agent-first control surface), I5 (deterministic gates decide — a driver is the only architecture where the deterministic component *runs* the gate instead of asking an LLM to), and I6 (the driver knows whether it merged, because it did it). A 3/10 constitutional score built on a misquoted ADR, one soft non-goal, and an explicitly-conceded non-collision with T1 is not defensible.

attacks.claim_attacked: "Hard enforcement must live in arm's own verbs and write doors, which is equally available under either architecture." (Option B rationale, and the load-bearing claim that seams suffice.)
attacks.refutation: This is false, and the evidence block refutes it in its own `known_gaps` list. Under Option B the enforcement code runs inside a process the untrusted party controls: "State machine transitions not gated — model can call arm claim, arm transition --to done … directly"; "Hook bypass via settings edit — model can edit .claude/settings.json or .claude/hooks/ to disable/modify hooks; Armature provides no mechanism to prevent hook modification"; "Out-of-band shell escapes — operations run via bare bash are never hooked; model can run 'sh -c'"; "Symlink-escape coverage gap"; "Unbound file writes … fail-open." A write door only guards a door someone walks through. There is no arm verb to harden against `sh -c 'git commit'`, and no verb-hardening that survives the agent editing the hook config. A driver moves the trust boundary out of the agent's process entirely — that is not a difference in degree, it is the only mechanism in play that changes who holds the boundary. The draft's own supporting citation is fatal to it: ADR 0007 and docs/harness-hook.md make the hook "a best-effort guardrail, not a sandbox." The draft quotes that to argue enforcement must move to verbs; the same sentence argues it must move out of the agent's process.

attacks.claim_attacked: "D-without-launch … makes the state derivable from git without anyone invoking anything, which is the half that closes the 'never typed arm merged' failures."
attacks.refutation: Derivable is not derived, and the corpus contains the controlled experiment. `2026-08-23T1930Z-codex-validation-stable-merged-status-audit.md` is exactly the content-based derivation the draft proposes — and it found ARCHIMP-S15 only when a human happened to run it during unrelated branch cleanup, months late. The capability existing did not cause it to run. Stage 1 has the same shape: `arm sync` decides merged from git evidence *when invoked*, and the theme the draft leans hardest on says "We cannot rely on agents to run commands, even if we ask them to." That sentence does not distinguish `arm transition --branch` from `arm sync`; it indicts the invocation model as such. The draft applies the finding to the flag and exempts the verb. Worse, the session-recovery-gaps theme documents that the invoker is the least reliable component in the system: coordinating sessions are "abruptly terminated (e.g., via usage limits)" and the S10 restart shape is literally "the human keeps merging PRs, nothing runs `arm merged`, and the next session inherits three disagreeing records." D-without-launch is a design whose correctness depends on a process the corpus documents dying mid-flight. Only something with its own re-entrant loop closes that.

attacks.claim_attacked: "This was built … debugged … and deleted. The constitution was ratified after the kill. Per house convention, C requires an amending ADR, not a design doc." (Decisive-evidence pillar.)
attacks.refutation: The precedent is narrower than the draft's use of it. The removal doc's own decision line is: "Armature does not execute or supervise harnesses. Armature may expose enforcement commands that harness-native hooks invoke," and the Removed column is specific — "Armature chooses a harness, resolves its auth, launches it, supervises it, retries it." What was killed is a *supervisor with vendor adapters and auth resolution*. Nothing in that document forbids arm owning cwd pinning, branch derivation, commit mechanics, transition authority, or *executing the gate itself* — and the doc explicitly preserves "a clear path" for arm-side enforcement. The draft cites this text and then applies it to a design it does not cover. The "19 of 29 cancellations are its debris" figure is circular: cancellations are how a deleted subsystem's backlog gets cleaned up, so the debris is caused by the kill, not evidence for it. And the ADR-required framing cuts the other way — the draft's own Stage 3 proposes writing exactly that ADR, so the objection is scheduling, not principle.

attacks.claim_attacked: "The highest-severity class survives both architectures … the LLM authors the tests and the gates run them green under either driver." (Pillar two.)
attacks.refutation: True about authorship, false about detection, and the draft contradicts itself two paragraphs later. Its own strongest positive finding is that the layered LLM review cascade caught P0s deterministic gates "structurally cannot see" (2026-07-20T0330Z, 2026-07-06T1500Z, 2026-07-06T1330Z), and its own recommendation is to "make the whole-story holistic pass a required pre-PR step rather than an optional one." *Required by what?* Under Option B, "required" is a skill sentence plus a verb someone must remember to type — the precise construction this entire corpus proves does not hold ("Do not treat a skill sentence as the close-the-loop step"). A driver makes it a step in a loop that cannot be skipped, with defined ordering and retry. Same for the cross-story patch-id content audit the draft wants. The class the draft calls untouchable-by-driver is the class whose only known mitigation is a scheduled, non-optional, non-agent-invoked review pass — which is a driver function. The draft also concedes without crediting that a driver running gates in an un-sandboxed parent fixes D8, the check that has been "always red" across three recurrences with no arm-side fix available.

attacks.claim_attacked: Score of 8/10 for Option B and 9/10 for D-without-launch, given the draft's own acknowledged treadmill.
attacks.refutation: The scores do not price the risks the draft itself lists. The git tallies: 384 fix commits against 390 feat — a near 1:1 ratio over 1190 commits — plus 52 hole-closing and 60 review-cycle-fix commits. LNGHZN-S4 cost 38 fix to 3 feat and produced *three distinct bypasses of the same gate inside nine days*; LNGHZN-S9-T1 cost 1 feat to 10 fix. The worker-worktree-bypass theme records seven recurrences over six weeks under escalating prose and escalating seams, and the latest instance (2026-08-15) is not disobedience at all — "the harness session's default cwd is the story tree … containment fails before the first instruction is read," which no verb-refusal can reach because no verb is invoked. This is a treadmill with a measured slope and no evidence of it flattening; the draft names it as risk #2 and then scores B/D as if it were not happening. A defensible verdict either shows the fix-per-seam ratio falling or discounts the score. It does neither.

attacks.claim_attacked: "Interactive harness sessions" as the home for dev work, with ordering and retry left implicit (D-without-launch mechanics, Stage 1-2).
attacks.refutation: The draft's own Stage 1 contains a self-refuting sentence: gate `arm merged` on assessment presence "**ordered before** worktree teardown so the command that discovers the gap does not also close the recovery window." That is a step-ordering guarantee — and under Option B/D-without-launch there is no place to express it except prose in a skill, which is the exact enforcement mechanism the draft spends its whole argument disqualifying. Interactive sessions provide no ordering, no idempotent retry, no resume-after-kill, and no at-most-once semantics; the corpus documents all four failing (haiku reviewers emitting three different invalid JSON shapes at a protocol boundary with no validate-and-retry; the coordinator hand-rolling parallel checkout+merge in one tree and contaminating two story branches; sessions dying to usage limits mid-wave). Retry semantics are a runtime property. You cannot obtain them by hardening a verb.

attacks.claim_attacked: The framing that Option C is a new, unproven architecture while Option A/B is the tested status quo.
attacks.refutation: Armature already runs a driver — it is written in prose and executed by an LLM. The coordinator skill is a state machine: survey DAG, dispatch wave, integrate, validate, close with PR. The evidence block's own reading of 2026-08-08 is decisive: "the deterministic coordinator-run make check was the de facto real gate every time … gates work when a non-LLM step actually runs them." The doc-drift cluster (2026-06-29T1823Z, 2026-06-30T2340Z, 2026-06-30T2345Z) is the same point from the other side: orchestration logic encoded as untestable markdown and shell pseudocode drifted from the CLI and from itself, repeatedly — a class that has no analogue when the loop is tested Go. So the real question is not "driver or no driver" but "is the driver written in a language with tests, types, and a compiler, or in prose that provably drifts." The draft never poses it, and by not posing it, gets to score the prose driver's costs as environmental rather than architectural.

survives: The core sentence — "no governance step may be optional-by-prompt; agents may drive work, they may not own facts" — survives completely and is the strongest thing in the draft. It is exactly the driver-advocate's premise, and the draft states it better than most of the corpus does.

The rejection of Option A survives without qualification. ARCHIMP-S15 recorded `merged` for code never on main, with arm validate 730/730 clean, is a constitutional falsification of I6 and the draft's source-level verification of the mechanism (no evidence check on the merged path in cmd/armature/transition.go; engine.go:228-236 assigning Branch/PR straight from the op payload; RunRollup at engine.go:589 aggregating rather than verifying) is correct and load-bearing.

Stage 0 survives entirely and should ship regardless of which option wins. Refusing `arm transition --to merged` without content-on-main evidence, making RunRollup verify, adding the merged-scope-on-origin/main doctor check, and killing `SkippedDeliveryGate:false` for a check that never executed are pure git facts, I5-clean, and equally required under a driver.

The third-value work — checked-true / checked-false / not-checked — survives and is arguably the draft's best original contribution. `internal/sync/sync.go:17` silently `continue`ing past MergeChecker errors and skipping done issues with empty Branch, producing "No merged branches detected" for eleven actually-merged PRs, is a reporting-honesty bug that a driver would inherit unchanged.

The seam-corrosion argument survives and is real: D8 always-red under sandbox across three recurrences, false-positive overlap warnings training 11 consecutive `--force` claims, ADR 0016's "fail-closed on paper, fail-open in practice." Badly-calibrated determinism is worse than none. This is a genuine constraint on any deterministic expansion, driver included.

Keeping the LLM review cascade survives, and the draft is right that no architecture replaces it — a driver can only schedule it. Holistic review finding P0s inside armature's own seam code (IsWithinScope and the ' (new)' annotation) is the cleanest evidence in the corpus that deterministic gates cannot self-validate.

The demand that theme follow-up lists be filed as one tracked epic with a burn-down survives and is well-argued: the record shows follow-up lists are where P0s go to wait, and that is precisely how ARCHIMP-S15 survived two months.
missing: No cost comparison in either direction. The draft never prices B/D's ongoing seam tax (384 fix vs 390 feat commits; 52 hole-closing; 38:3 on one story; three bypasses of one gate in nine days) against C's one-time build cost, despite naming the treadmill as a risk. A verdict rejecting an architecture on complexity grounds while measuring only the rejected side's complexity is incomplete.

No separation of Option C into its two independent halves. (a) arm owns the state-machine loop, cwd/branch/commit mechanics, transition authority, and gate execution; (b) arm invokes harnesses headlessly. Every objection the draft raises — N2, vendor adapters, auth resolution, API-key billing, the 2026-06 removal precedent — lands only on (b). (a) is never assessed on its own merits anywhere in the document, which is the single largest omission.

No treatment of the trust boundary as a first-class concept. The evidence block's known_gaps say plainly that the model can edit .claude/settings.json, escape via `sh -c`, and call `arm transition --to merged` directly. Whether enforcement runs inside or outside the untrusted party's process is the actual architectural question, and it is never named.

No retry, idempotency, or resume semantics anywhere. The session-recovery-gaps theme documents coordinating sessions dying to usage limits mid-wave and the first hour of every restart being reconstruct-not-implement; the haiku assessment-format finding calls for validate-and-retry treatment of LLM output as untrusted input. Neither B nor D-without-launch has a place to put retry policy.

No acknowledgment that the coordinator skill is already a driver, just one written in untested prose. The doc-drift cluster is direct evidence that prose-encoded orchestration logic drifts from the CLI and from itself; the draft cites the drift findings nowhere.

The product-target question is deferred to a risk bullet when it is dispositive. If the target is unattended or fleet operation, D-without-launch is structurally incapable and the draft says so — then recommends it anyway and schedules the decision for Stage 3. That ordering is backwards: the target determines the option, so it belongs before Stage 0, not after Stage 2.

No consideration of a partial driver as a migration path rather than a binary. `arm run --once` as a re-entrant, foreground, human-launched step function that pins cwd, makes the commit, runs the gate un-sandboxed, and derives the transition from what it actually observed — with harness launching left entirely outside — is available today, trips no tripwire, needs no vendor adapter, and has no billing surface. It is buried in Stage 3 behind a gate rather than assessed as an option.

No falsification criterion for the recommended path. Stage 3 defines one for Option C ("does a new class of protocol failure appear that cannot be closed by a refusal at a verb") but none for D-without-launch. Given that the worktree-bypass class has already survived seven recurrences and six weeks of escalating seams, that criterion arguably fires today.
skeptics.overall: The verdict's premise is right and its Stage 0 is unarguable, but its rejection of the driver rests on four pillars and two of them do not hold. The commercial pillar attributes a billing/addressable-market rationale to `docs/archive/orchestration/2026-06-03-remove-managed-execution-design.md` that the file does not contain — its recorded rationale is complexity and inversion of control, full stop — and the underlying API-key fact is a billing-mode note in the draft's own evidence bundle, explicitly labeled \"by design, not a restriction.\" The arithmetic pillar divides by 124 when 18 of those are positive findings; against actual problems a driver prevents 46 of 106 fully or partially — a majority, not the minority claimed. The constitutional pillar misquotes ADR 0005's phase-one scope as a standing prohibition and concedes T1 is clean in letter, leaving one soft non-goal. The deeper structural failure is that the draft never separates Option C's two halves: every surviving objection lands on headless model invocation, and none lands on arm owning the state-machine loop, cwd/commit mechanics, and gate execution. Meanwhile the recommended D-without-launch depends on a verb being invoked by a session the corpus documents dying to usage limits mid-wave, and its own Stage 1 needs a step-ordering guarantee it can only express as prose. The strongest evidence for a driver is in the draft's own citations: the 2026-08-08 finding that the coordinator-run `make check` was \"the de facto real gate every time,\" and the doc-drift cluster showing that the orchestration loop already exists — as untested markdown. The verdict should be qualified to: Stage 0 immediately and unconditionally; assess arm-owned mechanics without model launch as a first-class option now rather than at Stage 3; and settle the unattended-versus-attended product target before, not after, committing to an invocation-dependent control plane.

skeptics.lens: seam-advocate — steelman Option B (seam-hardened current architecture); attack the draft's reservations about it and its manufacture of "D-without-launch" as a distinct, better option

attacks.claim_attacked: Option D-without-launch is a distinct option scoring 9, one point above Option B, because 'B hardens verbs that an agent still has to invoke, while D additionally makes the state derivable from git without anyone invoking anything.'
attacks.refutation: The distinguishing property does not exist in the draft's own plan. Every Stage 0-2 item is a change to arm's verbs or data model: a refusal in cmd/armature/transition.go, a verification in RunRollup (internal/materialize/engine.go:589), a new doctor check, a third value in the data model, and a repair to internal/sync/sync.go. Every one requires someone to invoke arm. The draft admits this itself in risk #3 — 'someone must still call arm sync or arm merged' — which retracts the exact property the extra point was awarded for. Manufacturing a new option name for what is Option B's roadmap has a concrete cost: it keeps a driver-adjacent label ('D') alive in the decision record, and Stage 3 then re-opens the driver question under it. Name the verdict Option B; call Stages 0-2 what they are, B's burn-down.

attacks.claim_attacked: 'The harness hook cannot be the hard seam ... it does not intercept a model calling arm transition --to done directly' — used to justify B's 7/10 reliability and to establish the 'never invoked / wrongly invoked directly' residual class.
attacks.refutation: This conflates a matcher-configuration gap with a mechanism gap. The evidence block's own hook_today section lists as enforced today: 'Git commit blocking — hook denies direct git commit commands, forcing Armature-owned commit flow,' via PreToolUse exit code 2 on the Bash matcher, which the seam catalog describes as 'non-overridable — model cannot retry or ignore the denial.' internal/harnesspolicy (340 prod LOC) already inspects Bash command strings. If `git commit` can be denied by pattern, `arm transition --to merged` can be denied by pattern, today, with no new architecture. ADR 0007's fail-open posture applies to binding *resolution* failures, not to a matched deny. The draft's own qualification (hard enforcement must live in arm's verbs) is correct as a primary control and defense-in-depth, but stating the hook 'cannot' be a hard seam for this shape is factually wrong and it depresses B's score on a gap that is a config line.

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #2: 'Seam complexity may eventually exceed driver complexity. LNGHZN-S4 cost 38 fix commits to 3 feat ... If the fix-per-seam ratio does not fall, the whack-a-mole reading wins and the ORCRMV complexity verdict should be revisited.'
attacks.refutation: Measured, this inverts. The entire live enforcement stack is ~2,932 lines of production Go: internal/deliverygate 593, internal/harnesshook 1,613, internal/harnesspolicy 340, internal/scopematch 279, internal/commitref 72, internal/sync 35. The driver removal deleted 10,620 lines in two commits (70c0d3b5: 1,444 deletions; 45d05dfe: 9,176 deletions across 39 files). The driver's flattering commit ratio (30 feat / 9 fix across ORCRUN|ORCH-RUNTIME|E7-S1|ORCRMV, `git log`) is an artifact of its remediation being total deletion rather than incremental fix — you cannot count fix commits against a subsystem whose fix was `rm`. LNGHZN-S4's 36 fix commits are 36 fixes to a 593-line package that now blocks a whole failure class; and 34 of the 83 LNGHZN-S4 commits are `ops` state commits, not code. The risk as written should be struck, or restated as 'seam quality is a recurring defect source' — which the draft already says elsewhere and which is a review-discipline problem, not a complexity-crossover problem.

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #4 and Option C's 7/10 reliability: 'a driver would have absorbed some of this by running gates in an un-sandboxed parent — a real advantage this recommendation gives up' (the D8 case).
attacks.refutation: A driver does not fix D8, it relocates the gate into a different environment than the one the work happened in — which is precisely the wrong-checkout failure shape the LNGHZN-S4 delivery gate already burned on (2026-08-02T1600Z, SkippedDeliveryGate:false written from the wrong cwd). The repo's own theme names the actual fix and it is two bounded, in-architecture changes: 'CleanTree: honor .gitignore, matching git status --porcelain' and 'D8: rule only on paths the repository could plausibly own,' generalized as 'a deterministic gate should only rule on artifacts a worker can actually control' (docs/dogfood/findings/themes/sandbox-environment-vs-gates/README.md). The child harness session still injects the bind mounts under a driver; only the observation point moves, and moving it introduces a new class (gate ran somewhere the code was not). Conceding this as 'a real advantage given up' is unearned; it is a ~50-line seam fix the draft already schedules in Stage 2.

attacks.claim_attacked: Option A scored 3/10, 'actively unsafe, not merely suboptimal ... A is disqualified on its own constitution.'
attacks.refutation: The draft's own key evidence contains the counterweight and then does not price it: the stable whole-DAG audit against pinned hashes (origin/main 80dee97c, ops 07df325d) classified 569 merged records as 562 CONFIRMED_DELIVERY, 0 FALSE_MERGED, 7 NOT_DETERMINABLE, and explicitly found that 26 provisionally alarming mismatches were historical deliveries later removed or renamed (docs/dogfood/findings/raw/2026-08-23T1930Z-codex-validation-stable-merged-status-audit.md). One false family in ~570 is a P0 defect with a base rate near zero, and I2 append-only meant it was corrected by appending cancellations rather than rewriting anything. Scoring the status quo as constitutionally disqualified on a single-family defect whose fix the draft itself scopes at 'days' overstates the case — and overstating A's failure is what creates artificial headroom for C to score 4 on reliability grounds it does not deserve. A is 'has a shipped P0 and an unscheduled follow-up habit,' not 'architecturally void.'

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #3: 'If the actual product target is unattended autonomous runs ... D-without-launch is structurally insufficient ... In that world C or D-with-launch is correct and the constitution needs an amending ADR.'
attacks.refutation: False dichotomy that quietly re-licenses the tripwire. Unattended operation requires that *something* invoke arm on a schedule; it does not require arm to launch a model. cron, a CI job, or the 'thin external runner the user owns' the draft itself proposes in Stage 3 all satisfy it, and all keep N2, T1 and ADR 0005 intact because the constitution constrains armature, not the operator's crontab. The reconciliation-on-invocation pattern the draft cites approvingly (arm doctor --fix, materialization) is already idempotent and crash-safe, which is exactly what makes external scheduling safe. Writing 'the constitution needs an amending ADR' into the unattended branch converts a packaging question into a constitutional one and hands future readers a pre-authorized route back to C.

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #5: 'The recommendation does nothing about the highest-severity class ... If those dominate real-world cost, the entire driver-versus-seams debate is second-order and the correct investment is review architecture rather than either option under assessment.'
attacks.refutation: Mis-assigned. The false-green class is where seams have the corpus's only demonstrated wins and where the fix is explicitly seam-shaped. The unreliable-worker-self-report theme's own candidate follow-up is mechanical: 'A done-time check that the contracted _REQ_<ID> test names are present in the diff would close shape 3 mechanically, since the names are already declared in the acceptance array.' The citation validator already converted fabrication into a blocked operation (2026-06-29T1915Z, line 104 of an 87-line diff). Contract-mandated _REQ_ names already surfaced a real path bug on LNGHZN-S3-T1. And 'review architecture' is not a third option outside the assessment — mandatory pre-PR holistic review is a gate, i.e. a seam, and the draft's own recommendation ends by making it one. Framing the P0 class as orthogonal to the debate understates that it is Option B's strongest scoring ground and Option C's weakest (a driver still runs LLM-authored hollow tests green).

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #6: 'A meaningful share of the protocol-failure class may be model-capability-bound ... Conversely, if the target deployment is cheap-model fleets, the protocol class is permanent and the driver case strengthens.'
attacks.refutation: The cheap-model branch is not symmetric, because the corpus already shipped the seam-side answer to it. 2026-06-29T1945Z records 3/3 haiku reviewers emitting structurally invalid assessment JSON three different ways while sonnet was valid first-try — and the effective-patterns theme identifies the differentiator explicitly as 'a concrete verbatim JSON template in the prompt (field names, bracket-notation criterion IDs, schema_version: 1),' not the model tier alone. The general treatment the evidence prescribes is validate-and-retry on LLM output as untrusted input — a schema seam at a protocol boundary, available today, and mandatory under either architecture since a driver receives the same malformed JSON. The cheap-model branch therefore strengthens the case for typed, validated seams at every LLM boundary; it does not differentially strengthen C.

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #7: 'Consolidating control-plane authority in arm concentrates blast radius ... a deterministic promoter that derives merged from patch-id comparison across the whole DAG can be wrong systematically and silently.'
attacks.refutation: True in shape, but the severity is bounded by properties the draft does not credit and that a driver does not have. Derived promotion writes ops, and I2 append-only means every wrong derivation is re-derivable, auditable, and correctable by appending — which is exactly how ARCHIMP-S15 was fixed. The codex audit is the existence proof that a whole-DAG content check can be run, stabilized across two passes on pinned hashes, and preserve NOT_DETERMINABLE rather than collapsing to a confident value. A driver, by contrast, performs irreversible git side effects (branch creation, commits, merges) — the 2026-06-27T0003Z parallel checkout race contaminated two story branches — where being systematically wrong is not append-only correctable. The risk should be retained but qualified: blast radius concentration is real for *records*, and strictly worse under C for *repositories*.

attacks.claim_attacked: Risk #8: 'If the tax is overstated, A is less damning than the synthesis presents.'
attacks.refutation: Directionally under-drawn. If the ~27% hardening-tax figure is soft — and the evidence block concedes 'much of the remaining ~72% IS agent-governance functionality — it is the product armature set out to be' — then the primary *quantitative* case that prompted driving is expensive weakens, which removes the main cost argument for rebuilding a driver, not merely the main indictment of A. Stated only as a mitigation for A, the risk hides that it is also a deduction from C.

survives: The governing rule — 'no governance step may be optional-by-prompt; agents may drive work, they may not own facts' — survives every attack and is the correct single-sentence output of the corpus. The i6-promotion theme's verbatim 5-whys ('We cannot rely on agents to run commands, even if we ask them to') and the worker-worktree-bypass verdict ('Prose does not fix it') are unimpeachable.

The rejection of Option C survives intact and is if anything under-argued. The natural-experiment record is decisive: E7-S1 built it, ORCRUN spent 19 issues fixing its contract, ORCRMV deleted 10,620 lines across 41 files (70c0d3b5, 45d05dfe), the recorded rationale was 'excessive complexity,' the standing non-goal forbids a replacement run/execute/dispatch command, and ADR 0009 ratified the constitution *after* the kill. My measurements strengthen this, not weaken it.

Stage 0 is right and urgent, and its scope is even smaller than the draft implies: internal/sync/sync.go is 35 lines of production code containing both silent `continue`s that produced 'No merged branches detected' for eleven merged PRs. RunRollup's aggregation is one loop in internal/materialize/engine.go. These are hours-to-days fixes, which is itself an argument that the P0 indicts a defect, not an architecture.

The observation that seams ruling on facts agents cannot control actively corrode enforcement (D8 always-red, false-positive overlap training habitual --force, ADR 0016's 'fail-closed on paper, fail-open in practice') is the single best-supported design constraint in the draft and should be elevated from a caveat to a normative rule for all future seams.

Keeping the LLM review cascade untouched, and making the whole-story holistic pass a required pre-PR gate, survives. The effective-patterns theme documents the haiku→opus/fable→sonnet cascade succeeding across 10+ runs and repeatedly outproducing the literal findings, including finding defects inside armature's own gate code.

Risk #1 (reactive seams degrading into A with better intentions) survives as the strongest real reservation, though it understates the convergence record: heartbeats prose→hook, PR discipline prose→transition gate, gate results prose→hash-anchored evidence ops, warnings→errors with escape hatches deleted, and LNGHZN-S4's wrong-checkout bypass fixed the day it was found (83bb221c). Reactive-and-converging is a different disease from reactive-and-stalling.
missing: The single cheapest available hard seam is never assessed: a PreToolUse Bash matcher denying `arm transition --to merged` (and gating `--to done`) exactly as `git commit` is denied today via internal/harnesspolicy. The draft asserts the hook 'cannot' be the hard seam for CLI invocations while the evidence block lists command-pattern denial as already shipped. This belongs in Stage 0 as defense-in-depth behind the verb-level refusal.

No defect-prevented-per-line ranking of candidate seams, which is what would actually answer the complexity worry. internal/sync at 35 prod LOC produced a P0-class reporting failure; internal/commitref at 72 prod LOC underwrites the delivery gate. Ordering Stage 0-2 by this ratio would make the burn-down defensible rather than aspirational.

I2 append-only is never named as a *safety* property of the seam architecture. ARCHIMP-S15 was corrected without rewriting history; the audit re-derived 569 records from two pinned hashes and got the same answer twice. Recoverability-by-append is a structural advantage the seam path has and a driver's irreversible git operations do not, and it belongs in the option comparison rather than only in the constitution section.

No proposed metric for the reactive-seam risk. The third-value work (checked-true / checked-false / not-checked) makes 'what fraction of this record is actually checked' computable — `arm validate` could report check-coverage per issue. That converts risk #1 from a worry into a tracked number with a burn-down, which is the only thing that would prove the plan is not A with better intentions.

The review-evidence-stranded-on-GitHub finding (2026-08-23T1538Z) is cited as a 'never invoked' example but no seam is proposed for it, despite being trivially seam-shaped: gate `arm merged` on presence of a .armature/review assessment, which the draft does propose in Stage 1 but does not connect back to this finding — and does not consider having the review cascade itself write the evidence op rather than relying on a human to record it.

No treatment of what the 7 NOT_DETERMINABLE records imply for the plan. The audit's own suggested follow-up — 'persist deterministic gate attestations keyed by invoking checkout, commit, command, and result' — is the direct fix for both the 'ran a subset of make check' class and the future-auditability problem, and it is a pure seam. It should be a Stage 1 line item; the draft omits it.

No cost estimate on the other side of the ledger: what Stages 0-2 would cost in LOC and stories versus the ~10.6k lines the driver cost before deletion. Without that number the 'seam complexity may exceed driver complexity' risk stays unfalsifiable.
skeptics.overall: The draft reaches the right destination and then hedges its way partly back toward the thing it just rejected. Its rejection of Option C is sound and under-argued in its own favor; its indictment of Option A is overstated on a defect with a measured base rate of one family in ~570; and its headline option, "D-without-launch," is Option B with a new letter — the draft concedes the two are "close to indistinguishable" and then contradicts the only property it names as distinguishing ("without anyone invoking anything") three paragraphs later in risk #3. The practical harm of that renaming is not cosmetic: it keeps a driver-shaped label in the decision record and gives Stage 3 a friendly on-ramp back to C, plus a risk section that twice ("in that world C or D-with-launch is correct", "the ORCRMV complexity verdict should be revisited") pre-authorizes re-litigation the evidence does not support. Measured rather than asserted, the complexity argument runs strongly the other way: the entire live enforcement stack is ~2,900 production lines against 10,620 deleted in the driver removal, and the driver's flattering fix-commit ratio is an artifact of its remediation being deletion. Recommended changes: name Option B as the verdict and Stages 0-2 as its burn-down; delete or invert risk #2 on the measured LOC evidence; downgrade risk #4 to "fix the gate, don't move it" per the repo's own stated principle; rewrite risk #3 so unattended operation is a packaging question (cron / CI / user-owned runner) rather than a constitutional one; re-file risk #5 as Option B's strongest scoring ground rather than a wash; add the PreToolUse Bash-matcher deny on `arm transition --to merged` to Stage 0; add durable gate attestations to Stage 1; and add a check-coverage metric so risk #1 — the one reservation that fully survives — becomes measurable instead of hortatory.

attacks.claim_attacked: Stage 1: gate `arm merged` on conformance-assessment presence "with `--i7-override --reason` as the only bypass" — presented as I7-accountable break-glass.
attacks.refutation: /home/brian/development/armature/docs/adr/0016-three-door-validation.md:69 says verbatim: "Break-glass is a **Release Override**, not a flag on the agent verb." Lines 71-73 specify the actual template the draft claims to be following: `arm dag override-release` requires a controlling terminal (`/dev/tty`), records `skipped_validate_gate` plus the reason, and "success is never 'green.'" A `--i7-override --reason` pair on an agent verb is precisely the rejected shape, and this repo already has the empirical proof: `--force` (cmd/armature/claim.go:1572, and the draft's own citation of 11 consecutive `--force` claims on DF-S5) and `--skip-delivery-gate` (internal/deliverygate/basecommit.go:180) are agent-typed flags that got typed reflexively. The draft's governing rule is "no governance step may be optional-by-prompt"; its own bypass mechanism is optional-by-prompt, typeable by the same haiku worker that fabricated the ARCHIMP-S15 outcome. The recommendation reintroduces the hole it exists to close, while citing the ADR that forbids it.

attacks.claim_attacked: Option D is constitutionally clean (constitution_fit 8/10) and Stage 3 can pre-register `arm run --once` behind an N2/ADR-0005 amendment.
attacks.refutation: The draft cites docs/archive/orchestration/2026-06-03-remove-managed-execution-design.md against Option C but never quotes its Non-Goals section, line 58: "Do not add a replacement `run`, `execute`, `dispatch`, or handoff command." Line 41: "No replacement execution or handoff command will be added in this transition." The draft's own Option D is defined as covering "dispatch bookkeeping" and its Stage 3 names the verb `arm run --once`. Both forbidden nouns, used without acknowledgement. This is not fatal to D's substance — bookkeeping is not execution — but the constitutional accounting is wrong in two ways: (a) D must be renamed away from "dispatch" or explicitly distinguished from the parked verb, or the next agent reading the plan resuscitates the killed surface by name; (b) Stage 3 needs an amendment to the removal design's standing non-goal, not only to N2 and ADR 0005 as the draft states. The draft applies "cite the kill, don't re-argue" strictly to C and not at all to itself.

attacks.claim_attacked: D-without-launch "closes every failure in the 2026-08-23 corpus without touching a tripwire" and scores constitution 8/10; the recommendation's cross-cutting item makes "the whole-story holistic pass a required pre-PR step."
attacks.refutation: /home/brian/development/armature/docs/adr/0005-semantic-conformance-review-boundary.md states phase one "will not run models or customer checks inside Armature, use harness hooks or activity traces, retain full reports in Git, or block delivery on review results." Making holistic LLM review a *required* pre-PR step, and gating `arm merged` on a review artifact, both block delivery on review — the draft's own closing sentence concedes it is "the one place where a mandatory gate and LLM judgment should be deliberately combined." That admission is doing constitutional work the option scoring never pays for. Presence-not-rating is a defensible I5-safe line, but ADR 0005's prohibition is on blocking delivery on review at all, and ADR 0008 shows this repo's convention: narrowing 0005 requires an upgrade-only amending ADR, not a plan bullet. Verdict must be qualified: D requires its own amending ADR, so the "C needs an amendment, D doesn't" asymmetry that carries the recommendation is false as written.

attacks.claim_attacked: Fourth refutation pillar: "the commercial constraint that killed it the first time still holds: headless invocation requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not subscription auth" — used to score C commercial 3/10 and D 8/10.
attacks.refutation: The evidence block's own print_policy summary says the opposite of how it is deployed: "There is NO current documented restriction on --print itself when using API key authentication" and per-token billing under OAuth is "by design, not a restriction." Confidence is stated as **medium**, and the sourcing is two GitHub issue numbers (#36350, #43333) plus an unlinked "Anthropic policy update (2026)" with no URL — the weakest evidence in the entire corpus, carrying one of four stated pillars. Worse, the pillar is not differentiating: the draft's own cross-cutting mandate keeps an LLM review cascade and makes holistic review required. The only thing keeping that on subscription billing rather than API billing is a human sitting in an interactive harness session — which the draft's risk #3 concedes is a product-positioning assumption "the evidence cannot settle." So the commercial argument against C is the human-present assumption wearing a billing costume, not an independent refutation. Strike it or re-score it; C's rejection survives on the ORCRMV/N2/ADR-0005 record alone, which is where the draft should have rested it.

attacks.claim_attacked: D preserves I7 ("I7 helped"; "N4 is respected because the PR merge stays human and armature only records confirmed facts"), and Stage 1's goal is to "close the loop without an agent typing anything."
attacks.refutation: CONSTITUTION.md I7: "Accountability for merges, releases, and **overrides** never transfers to the system — no matter how reliably it functions." Stage 1 explicitly deletes the last per-issue human-or-agent attestation for `merged` and replaces it with derivation by arm code. A human merging a PR on GitHub is accountable for the *merge*; nobody is then accountable for the *merged record*, which is the artifact I6 governs and the exact artifact that was fiction in ARCHIMP-S15. The draft's own risk #7 concedes a derived promoter "can be wrong systematically and silently" at DAG scale. Trading an agent-authored false record for a program-authored one at higher blast radius is not an I7 improvement; it is accountability diffusion with better provenance. D needs a named human attestation point — an ADR-0016-shaped periodic reconciliation acceptance, or a doctor-surfaced derived-vs-recorded diff a human clears — before Stage 1's automation is constitutional rather than merely convenient.

attacks.claim_attacked: The four-stage ordering: Stage 1 ships derived promotion; Stage 2 introduces the third value (checked-true / checked-false / not-checked).
attacks.refutation: The draft's own risk #7 states: "The third-value work in Stage 2 is a precondition for Stage 1, not a follow-on." The plan then ships them in the contradicted order. Concretely: the codex whole-DAG audit found 7 NOT_DETERMINABLE merged records for lack of durable gate attestation, and patch-id comparison has real indeterminate cases (conflict-resolved squashes, amended commits, rebased-and-fixed-up merges). A Stage-1 promoter without a not-checked value must render every one of those as a two-valued answer — reproducing `DetectMerges`' "No merged branches detected" over eleven merged PRs (internal/sync/sync.go:17), the exact defect class Stage 1 claims to fix. The recommendation is internally inconsistent on its own critical path.

attacks.claim_attacked: "T3 is respected because sync stays pull-only, deciding from git evidence at invocation time rather than watching a mutable remote."
attacks.refutation: T3 reads "syncs bidirectionally with a mutable remote." Pull-only answers direction, not mutability — and mutability is the live problem. Deriving `merged` from origin/main content makes a core constitutional state fact a function of a remote armature does not control and cannot pin. A force-push, a squash rewrite, or branch-protection changes on GitHub flip the derivation after the fact; under I2 ("history is never rewritten") the local op log is stable while its truth-conditions are not. The draft never states whether derived promotions are appended as ops (I2-safe, but then stale) or recomputed each run (fresh, but silently demotable). Risk #4 identifies vendor-controlled ground moving under deterministic gates via the D8 case and then does not apply that lesson to the promoter, which is the most consequential derivation in the plan.

attacks.claim_attacked: Cross-harness viability: the recommendation is implicitly portable because it lives in arm's verbs.
attacks.refutation: True for the arm-side half only; the plan's other half is Claude-shaped. Stage 2 proposes making doctor's D8 "sandbox-aware" — encoding one vendor's bind-mount semantics into a deterministic gate. The mandatory holistic-review step, heartbeat capture, and the PreToolUse exit-code-2 block the draft leans on in key_evidence all rest on hook semantics that differ across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI, which AGENTS.md deploys skills to equally (.claude/, .gemini/, .codex/). docs/harness-hook.md makes hook resolution deliberately fail-open, and ADR 0016 already rejected "a harness hook as the primary control (Claude-shaped; I5)." A "required" step that only binds where a hook exists is optional-by-prompt on two of three supported harnesses — the draft's own governing rule failing on the majority of its harness surface. The plan needs a per-harness enforcement matrix, or every mandate must be reduced to a refusal inside an arm verb.

attacks.claim_attacked: Stage 0 option (1): "`arm transition --to merged` refuses without content-on-main evidence, or the path is removed entirely."
attacks.refutation: The removal branch triggers /home/brian/development/armature/docs/adr/0010-park-not-purge-subtractive-release.md, which permits outright deletion but binds it to a mechanical obligation the draft omits: the only permitted record of a park is a census row in docs/design/subtractive-release.md carrying the ruling and a re-entry criterion, plus the removing commit — and "a park PR that leaves runtime traces does not satisfy this ADR." Removing a documented user-facing transition path without the census row is a purge, which 0010 reserves for surfaceless dead code. Small, but this is exactly the kind of unrecorded governance step the draft's own thesis says becomes fiction later.

survives: The rejection of Option C survives my attack cleanly, and survives it better without the commercial leg: docs/archive/orchestration/2026-06-03-remove-managed-execution-design.md:29 ("Armature does not execute or supervise harnesses") and :58 (no replacement run/execute/dispatch/handoff), ADR 0005's "will not run models... inside Armature," and ADR 0009 ratifying N2/T1 *after* the ORCRMV kill are sufficient on their own. C is a constitutional-amendment request, not a design question.

D-without-launch does not trip T1, T2, or T3 as written. Discrete, idempotent, human- or session-invoked commands that terminate and hold no state outside git ops are behaviorally indistinguishable from `arm doctor --fix` and materialization, both of which the constitution already tolerates. I1's "no daemon" is not strained by the recommendation as described.
N4 is respected in the narrow sense that matters: the merge decision stays with a human on GitHub; arm records rather than authorizes.

The governing rule — "no governance step may be optional-by-prompt; agents may drive work, they may not own facts" — is a fair generalization of ADR 0003's stochasticity premise and is not constitutional overreach. It is the strongest sentence in the draft.
Presence-never-rating is the correct I5-safe shape for any review-linked gate, and the draft holds that line explicitly. My attack is on ADR 0005's separate no-blocking-on-review clause, not on I5.

The arm-side control plane is genuinely vendor-neutral: it rules on git facts, not harness APIs, which is the one place the plan is portable across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI without adapters.
missing: No market is ever named. Commercial viability is scored 3-8/10 across four options with no stated buyer, pricing model, distribution channel, or competitor. "Commercial 8/10" for D is unfalsifiable, and the only concrete commercial input in the whole analysis is a medium-confidence billing claim.

No amendment-cost ledger. The draft demands an amending ADR for C and implies D needs none, but D as recommended amends ADR 0005 (blocking on review) and brushes the removal design's non-goals. Until both columns are filled in, the constitutional cost comparison that decides the verdict is not apples-to-apples.

I3 is never analyzed for a reconciler. Which worker's log receives derived promotion ops? What happens when two operators run `arm sync` concurrently over the same issues? Idempotency is asserted and never specified, and I3's "each worker writes exclusively to its own log file" is the invariant that makes armature merge-conflict-free.

N5 ("not a human-first PM suite") is never tested against the plan's growing reporting surface — "count what you looked at," "N done issues skipped: no branch recorded," doctor audits, burn-down epic. Each is individually justified; nobody checks the aggregate against N5.

I7 in a multi-operator repo. The corpus is one operator; the constitution says humans own outcomes but never says which human. Any override or reconciliation-acceptance design needs a named accountable party, and the plan assumes a singular one.

Distribution-shape pressure on T1/I1. If armature is ever offered hosted, or invoked from CI on a schedule, the long-running process returns through the product rather than the code. The draft treats T1 as a property of the binary; it is a property of the deployment.

Whether the constitution should be amended at all. Every option is scored against Version 1 as fixed law, yet the draft's own risk #8 says the product boundary itself may be wrong. "Amend I5/N2 deliberately" is a fifth option that was never placed on the table.
skeptics.overall: The verdict direction survives — reject C on the recorded kill, reject A on I5/I6, adopt a hardened deterministic control plane that never launches a model — but three of the supports it rests on do not. The commercial pillar against C is medium-confidence, thinly sourced, and reduces to the human-present assumption the draft itself flags as unsettled; it should be struck rather than scored. The claimed constitutional asymmetry between C and D is false as written, because D-as-recommended also needs an amending ADR (ADR 0005's no-blocking-on-review clause) and reuses two verbs the removal design forbids by name. And the plan's own break-glass, `--i7-override --reason`, is verbatim the shape ADR 0016:69 rejected — an optional-by-prompt flag on an agent verb, in a plan whose thesis is that nothing may be optional-by-prompt. Fix those three and the recommendation stands; leave them and it is a well-argued verdict with a bypass flag drilled through it. On the narrow lens questions: T1 and I1 are not tripped; N2 is not strained by D-without-launch but is strained by its naming; I7 is asserted rather than preserved once Stage 1 removes the last human attestation for `merged`; and cross-harness viability holds for the arm-side half only — every hook-, sandbox-, or skill-mediated mandate in the plan is Claude-shaped and therefore advisory on Codex CLI and Gemini CLI.
